market_holds: Spot $4.63 (sealed baseline 2026-11-19 18:08 UTC), at its 52-week low and -55% from the high. The stock was down 46% from its $8.64 close before the Q2 print (Yahoo daily bars), -24% over 20 sessions and -6.7% over 5. Front-week straddle implies 8.5%, ATM IV 141%. Calls are bid over puts (25d skew -16 vol points) and put/call OI is 0.17, so retail is positioned long. Short interest was 41.6m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (~5-6% of float, 3 days to cover). Consensus for Q3: EPS ~$0.06, revenue ~$216.5M (Benzinga) to $222.7M (Chartmill), revised up ~17% over 3 months, so the full-quarter effect of ending the PDT rule is largely modelled. No company guidance. The fall since August has its own causes: insider/10b5-1 sales and an F-3 resale registration (September), the House China committee report on 2026-10-07 (-19% that day on 81m shares), the FINRA $4.2M fine on 2026-11-05, and in November a sector-wide fintech/crypto selloff (HOOD -31% over the same 20 sessions, so BULL has lagged the sector less badly than HOOD). Last reactions: Q2'26, a big beat, was +13% premarket and closed +2.4%. Q3'25, a big beat, was about -2.7% after hours. Q1'26 is reported both ways. Q4'25 was a miss and fell.
view: On operations this quarter should be clean. It is the first full quarter without the PDT rule, and the best counterparty read, Robinhood's Q3 (options contracts 774M to 905M, +17% q/q; equity notional +4% q/q), matches management's own August remarks: options steady in July, equities softer than a SpaceX-heavy June, August stronger, margin balances near records. Applying those ratios to Webull's Q2 trading revenue of $147.7M gives about $170M. Add interest of ~$44M (Robinhood's NII was +7% q/q) and other income plus prediction markets of ~$10M, and total revenue comes to about $224M. That is at or slightly above a consensus that has already been raised for PDT. Marketing was guided flat to H1 levels, so EPS probably beats $0.06. Unlike Q2, when PDT was not in the numbers and revenue beat by 10-14%, this beat is likely small. The stock has also stopped trading on reported quarters: it fell 46% after a record quarter, on China ties, insider supply and the sector tape. What could move it at the open is the call: what management says about Q4-to-date activity (Robinhood's October ADVs were 4-7% below the Q3 average, and November has been risk-off), anything new on the House report or regulatory inquiries, and whether the $100M buyback gets used or expanded at a price half of April's. Crypto is about 1% of revenue, so the crypto selloff behind Robinhood's November slide barely touches Webull's numbers. That is a small mispricing the call could correct. Against it, a crowded long-call book and heavy political overhang make the reaction to an in-line beat hard to read. Net: slightly positive, nowhere near a bet.
unpriced: Possibly a small amount. Webull has trailed in the sector-wide fintech sell-off driven by crypto, yet its own crypto exposure is negligible (~1% of revenue), and at ~$2.3B market cap it is on roughly a mid-teens multiple of the run-rate earnings Q3 should show. That gap is valuation, not a visible miss in the estimate. Consensus already holds the PDT volume uplift, so I cannot show that the line the stock will trade on (Q4-to-date commentary, China/regulatory, buyback) lands above what the price holds.

recommendation.reason: Counterparty volumes (Robinhood Q3 options +17% q/q) and management's own July/August remarks point to Q3 revenue of about $224M, at or modestly above a consensus that was already raised ~17% for the PDT effect. So the beat is likely small and mostly modelled. The stock has decoupled from reported results since August and trades on China/regulatory headlines and the sector tape, and past beats have reacted both ways. Nothing in the evidence puts the deciding line, the Q4-to-date commentary and the regulatory tone, on one side by enough to clear 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A buyback executed in size or expanded, plus Q4-to-date volumes described as at or above Q3, would make the upside case. New disclosure of a US regulatory inquiry or investigation tied to the China report, or a legal/regulatory reserve hitting GAAP EPS, would make the downside case.

self_critique: The case for higher: the stock is at all-time-low territory with long-call positioning and a probable beat on both lines, so even a modest beat plus a buyback or upbeat Q4-to-date remarks could gap it up 10%+ at the open, as Q2 did premarket. My 56 may be too timid. The case for lower: consensus already holds the PDT uplift; Robinhood's October ADVs are below Q3, so Q4 commentary may sound like deceleration; the House report could bring new risk language or reserves; and the sector tape is in a hard risk-off phase that could swamp the print at the open. These two cases roughly cancel, which is why I stay close to 50 and make no call.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: HOOD fell more than BULL over 20 days, which showed the November drop was tape and not company news. P4 stopped me treating the 46% fall as a cushion. Counterparty arithmetic (P3) gave a usable revenue estimate, but with consensus already revised up it could not separate the deciding line, so P7's 65 bar correctly kept me out.
